title: N-Queens
source: canonical N-Queens concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: Place n queens on an n by n board so that no two share a row, column, or diagonal; exactly one queen sits in each row. Return every distinct solution as a list of boards, where each board is a list of n strings made of "Q" and "." characters. Sort the list of boards ascending so the output is deterministic.

examples.explanation: The 4 by 4 board has exactly two placements.
The 6 by 6 board has four placements.

hints: One queen per row is forced, so the search is over columns: pick a column for row 0, then row 1, and so on.
Columns and both diagonal directions need their own occupancy marks; row minus col and row plus col each identify a diagonal.
Backtrack: mark, recurse into the next row, unmark. Render a board whenever the last row is placed, then sort at the end.
solution: Backtracking row by row with column, diagonal, and anti-diagonal occupancy marks: each placement check is O(1), and boards render when all rows are placed. O(n!) search nodes with O(n) work each; output sorted for determinism.
solutionCode:
def solve_n_queens(n):
    solutions = []
    columns = [False] * n
    diagonals = [False] * (2 * n)
    anti = [False] * (2 * n)
    rows = []
    def place(row):
        if row == n:
            solutions.append(["." * col + "Q" + "." * (n - col - 1) for col in rows])
            return
        for col in range(n):
            d = row - col + n
            a = row + col
            if columns[col] or diagonals[d] or anti[a]:
                continue
            columns[col] = diagonals[d] = anti[a] = True
            rows.append(col)
            place(row + 1)
            rows.pop()
            columns[col] = diagonals[d] = anti[a] = False
    place(0)
    return sorted(solutions)
